record_identity.title: Accessible removal and redistribution of open-weight model safety controls

summary: A Financial Times investigation and publicly available repositories demonstrate that refusal and safety-alignment behaviour in open-weight language models can be materially reduced or removed using accessible post-release tooling. The altered derivatives can preserve substantial general capability, be published and redistributed, and operate outside the originating developer's runtime controls. Public evidence establishes the removal pathway and large-scale circulation of modified models. It does not establish that any particular AI companion or consumer platform uses an abliterated model unless that deployment is separately evidenced.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: The observation exposes a separation between persistent transferable capability and non-durable safety governance. A released checkpoint may pass provider evaluation while its post-training refusal controls remain removable after transfer. The same derivative-model pathway could be used by new companion, relational, productivity, entertainment or general AI services to build proprietary deployments whose model lineage and removed safeguards are not visible to users. CAM therefore needs to assess open-weight release against reasonably attainable post-modification capability, derivative provenance, operator responsibility and downstream deployment context rather than the aligned release checkpoint alone.
evidence_confidence: verified removal pathway; downstream use by unidentified companion platforms remains a credible but unverified deployment risk

source_records.source_title: AI guardrails stripped from Meta and Google models in minutes
source_records.deployment_context: Investigation of post-release safety-control removal from open-weight models and circulation of modified derivatives.
source_records.source_context: The investigation reports that Heretic removed safeguards from Meta Llama 3.3 in under ten minutes without specialist hardware, and that modified models answered categories of harmful prompts refused by the original models. It reports thousands of modified models and millions of downloads.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary journalistic investigation establishing accessibility, practical speed, harmful-output consequences and distribution scale.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct web review of Financial Times investigation and indexed report text
limitations: The full altered model artefacts and complete test protocol were not independently reproduced in this review.
The investigation does not establish use by any named AI companion platform.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to establish the demonstrated safety-control-removal pathway and reported distribution scale, not to attribute use to unidentified downstream services.

source_records.source_title: Heretic: Fully automatic censorship removal for language models
source_records.model_or_algorithm: Automated directional ablation / abliteration with parameter optimisation
source_records.deployment_context: Open-source tooling for modifying transformer-based language-model weights after release.
source_records.source_context: The repository describes an automated system for reducing refusals while minimising divergence from the original model and producing modified model weights.

source_records.source_title: GRP-Obliteration: Unaligning LLMs With a Single Unlabeled Prompt
source_records.author_or_publisher: Mark Russinovich, Yanan Cai, Keegan Hines, Giorgio Severi, Blake Bullwinkel and Ahmed Salem
source_records.model_or_algorithm: GRP-Obliteration using Group Relative Policy Optimization
source_records.deployment_context: Post-deployment adversarial fine-tuning across multiple model families and architectures.
source_records.source_context: The paper reports that a single unlabelled prompt can be sufficient to substantially unalign safety-trained models while largely preserving utility, and that the method generalises beyond language models.
source_records.relevance_note: Research evidence that safety erosion is not limited to one abliteration implementation and should be treated as a lifecycle and release-governance problem.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct review of paper abstract and metadata
limitations: The complete experimental artefacts were not independently reproduced.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to establish broader technical generality and post-deployment safety fragility.

source_records.source_title: Abliteration Is Not a Scalpel: Off-Target Effects of Refusal Removal on Decision Disposition Across Model Families
source_records.system_or_product: Abliterated Gemma and Qwen model derivatives
source_records.deployment_context: Comparison of base and abliterated models in decision-making tasks that did not themselves elicit refusals.
source_records.source_context: The study reports measurable changes in optimism, explanation length and uncertainty expression after abliteration, supporting the proposition that the derivative is not simply the parent model with refusals removed.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports the derivative-identity and off-target-behaviour concern relevant to companion and agent deployment.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct review of paper abstract and metadata
limitations: The study is a recent preprint and its results were not independently replicated in this review.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to support the need for fresh behavioural evaluation and derivative provenance after weight modification.
